title: Diagnostic optical coherence tomography findings in arteritic posterior ischemic optic neuropathy: A case report

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Diagnostic optical coherence tomography findings in arteritic posterior ischemic optic neuropathy: A case report》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0030】When assessing sudden onset visual loss in elderly patients, underlying giant cell arteritis (GCA) is an essential diagnosis to consider. GCA is associated with various ocular ischemic disorders, most notably arteritic ischemic optic neuropathy (A-ION).1 The anterior variant (A-AION) of A-ION is far more common than the posterior variant (A-PION), which constitutes only around 8-10% of A-ION cases.1, 2 In A-AION, optic disc edema is always present and on optical coherence tomography (OCT), paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) has been suggested as a specific biomarker of underlying GCA when differentiating from nonarteritic AION (NA-AION).3, 4

【Introduction · p0035】As there is no optic disc edema in A-PION, diagnosis is difficult and usually only established retrospectively, once optic atrophy has developed. However, in A-ION, time is of the essence. High dose corticosteroid therapy should be initiated immediately upon suspicion of GCA to reduce the risk of bilateral ocular involvement.1 It is therefore of utmost importance to find early clinical signs of ocular ischemia, when confronted with a putative case of A-PION.

【Case report · p0050】A 67-year-old man presented with sudden onset vision loss in the right eye. The visual loss initially involved only the inferior visual field but progressed to the entire visual field within 2 days of onset. Systemically, the patient reported no accompanying symptoms including absence of any headache, scalp tenderness, jaw or tongue claudication, proximal muscle pain, fatigue, loss of appetite, weight loss, fever or any neurological deficits. Prior to the event, the patient had no history of eye disease, while history of systemic disease included mild chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and HLA-B27 positive ankylosing spondylitis.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Diagnostic optical coherence tomography findings in arteritic posterior ischemic optic neuropathy: A case report》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · p0115】This case demonstrates that PAMM on macular OCT may occasionally be the only indication of GCA in a patient presenting with sudden vision loss. There is increasing evidence to support that macular OCT should be routinely performed in patients above 50 years presenting with acute vision loss, and that the finding of PAMM should prompt urgent and thorough investigation for GCA and consideration of initiating high-dose corticosteroid therapy, even in the absence of classic diagnostic features.

【Conclusion · abstract-3-1】PAMM on macular OCT may occasionally be the only indication of GCA in patients with sudden vision loss. Concurrent findings of PAMM and ischemic optic neuropathy in patients aged 50 and above should prompt urgent investigation for GCA and consideration of initiating treatment with high-dose corticosteroids, even without classic diagnostic features.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Diagnostic optical coherence tomography findings in arteritic posterior ischemic optic neuropathy: A case report》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · fig1】Fig. 1 A-E Imaging findings in the affected right eye at presentation. A: Fundus photograph with a cotton wool spot (CWS), slight narrowing of the arterioles, and no optic disc edema. B: Macular optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) (arrows) and a CWS (asterisk). C: En-face view of macular OCT at the level of the inner nuclear layer showing PAMM in a perivenular pattern. D: OCT through the center of the optic nerve head without optic disc edema. E: Indocyanine green angiography 31 seconds after injection revealing a nasal choroidal perfusion deficit. (For interpretation of the references to color in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the Web version of this article.)

【Fig. 2 · fig2】Fig. 2 A-B Vascular ultrasound of the right superficial temporal artery. A: Halo sign with color Doppler. B: Compression sign without Doppler with a combined artery wall thickness of 0.9 mm. (For interpretation of the references to color in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the Web version of this article.)

【Fig. 3 · fig3】Fig. 3 A-B The affected right eye 9 months after the ischemic event. A: Fundus photograph with a pale optic disc. B: Macular optical coherence tomography showing atrophy of inner retinal layers and multiple retinal ischemic perivascular lesions (RIPLs) (arrows).
